messages:
Sophia (AE): Team — Prospect Genomics wants to run a short Private POC. They've created their VPC and asked what we need for PrivateLink + egress for model inference. Need a plain-language checklist and a tiny Terraform snippet they can paste. Also they want to know if we can give a short-lived key scoped to the POC.
Omar (Solutions): Short checklist to send them: 1) Create an Interface VPCE to our service name (we'll send exact service_name and region). 2) Pick at least two subnets in different AZs for HA. 3) Attach a security group to the VPCE that allows inbound 443 from the application subnets. 4) Enable private_dns on the VPCE so api hostnames resolve privately. 5) Confirm they have NAT or ECR/S3 endpoints if their nodes need internet for images. 6) Share VPCE id + AWS account id with us so we can accept.
Lin (Infra): Add ops points: - We do not require/expect static outbound public IPs from customer for PrivateLink traffic. - If their environment requires egress through a firewall with allowlists, they need to allow outbound TLS to our service domain over the VPCE ENI IPs (these can change). - If they want to force egress via a single IP, they must proxy traffic through their own NAT box before hitting the VPCE (we don't provide a fixed egress IP).
Priya (Security): Security checklist: prefer Security Groups for access control. Do NOT try to use NACLs to restrict VPCE ENI traffic (NACLs are stateless and can break things). Verify TLS SNI is preserved — we terminate TLS on our certs; customer should not MITM. For scoped POC credentials: we can issue a time-limited API key (30d max) with model and rate restrictions; request via support ticket and include the customer's org name + intended models.
Sophia (AE): They asked about DNS: "If we enable private DNS, do we still need to add records to our private hosted zone?"
Omar (Solutions): In most cases no — enabling private_dns on the endpoint will cause the service hostname we provide to resolve to private IPs in their VPC. Only create private-hosted-zone records if they want a custom internal name (e.g., redwood.internal). In that case create a CNAME or ALIAS pointing to the VPCE DNS name.
Sophia (AE): Can you drop a tiny Terraform example they can adapt? Keep it minimal.
Omar (Solutions): Sure, share this snippet (they'll replace vpc/subnet ids and our service name):
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "rw_private_link" {
  vpc_id             = "vpc-0abcd1234"
  service_name       = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0123456789abcdef"
  vpc_endpoint_type  = "Interface"
  subnet_ids         = ["subnet-111","subnet-222"]
  security_group_ids = ["sg-allow-rw-vpce"]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}
```
Lin (Infra): Operational checklist for acceptance: once they create the VPCE post the vpce-id here, we'll check the acceptance queue, verify the service name matches, and confirm route/connectivity. We'll also ask them to run a quick connectivity test: `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health` from a bastion in the app subnet and paste the output.
Priya (Security): Also ask them to run `dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal` and show the private IPs. If it returns public IPs, private DNS isn't enabled.
Jordan (Sales): About billing/pricing: For the POC we can grant a small usage credit if needed; otherwise usage will bill at hosted rates. If they want a dedicated pool for the POC we can fast-track a small dedicated instance but that requires a short-term commitment.
Sophia (AE): Who will own the VPCE acceptance and scoped key creation?
Lin (Infra): I'll own the VPCE acceptance — ping me when vpce- is created.
Priya (Security): I'll coordinate the scoped key and policy with Support & Issuance team. Submit a ticket and tag me.
ops-bot: Created ticket RW-POC-772: "Genomics PrivateLink acceptance + POC scoped key" assigned to Lin and Priya.
Sophia (AE): Perfect — I'll send them the checklist + Terraform and ask for these: subnet IDs, account ID, vpce-id once created, and whether they need NAT for egress. Will set up a 20m handoff after they create the VPCE. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
